findings.title: V2 `canManage()` grants group management to holders of the all-groups `view` scope
findings.description:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, so a read-only all-groups `view` permission satisfies the manage check. The per-group overload at line 79 correctly checks only `MANAGE`.

- **Impact:** `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`GroupsResource.java:181`) is gated only by `auth.groups().requireManage()`. An admin with all-groups `view` can create top-level groups. With `rep.getId()` set, they can also move any existing group to the top level (`realm.moveGroup(child, null)` at line 198), with no per-group check.
- **Docs repeat the error:** the Javadoc at `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:72-78` says "VIEW or MANAGE" for `canManage()`.
- **No test catches it:** `testViewGroups` grants all-groups `VIEW` but never asserts that creating a group stays forbidden.
- **Fix:** check `MANAGE` only, correct the Javadoc, and add the negative assertion.

findings.title: V2 `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` confuses authz resource IDs with group IDs
findings.description:
The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource's own ID) to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` and adds the same value to the result. V2 resources carry the group ID in their name (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121`). The sibling `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` uses `resource.getName()` (line 140).

- **Wrong resource evaluated:** `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource id>)` at line 141 never matches, so every call falls through to the all-groups resource.
- **Wrong IDs returned:** the set feeds `UserModel.GROUPS` and `JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` (`groupId in (:groupIds)`) and the `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)` overloads, where resource IDs match no group.
- **All-groups case:** an admin with all-groups `view-members` or `manage-members` gets a non-empty set of non-group IDs, so the user list is filtered to nothing and the count is 0.
- **Per-group case:** per-group resources get no type in `getOrCreateResource` (lines 121-127), so `findByType(server, "Groups")` appears not to return them and the set stays empty. Listing then works only via the post-query `canView` filter (applied after pagination), while `/users/count` returns 0 (`JpaUserProvider.java:600`, `:635`, `:683`).
- **Untested:** the new tests cover only the per-group listing path; all-groups `view-members` and the count endpoint are not exercised.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource cannot be resolved
findings.description:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` when the schema is not supported for the realm or the type resource is missing (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:134-150`). The result goes straight into `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`, which dereferences `resource.getId()` (`StoreFactoryCacheSession.java:938`, `JPAPolicyStore.java:215`).

This is reachable when the admin-permissions client exists but `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false. The request then fails with a 500 instead of a clean deny. The same pattern already exists at `UserPermissionsV2.java:109-111`, but this change adds a copy on the group list and view paths. Add a null check that returns `false`.

findings.title: Feature flag for the cleanup listener is now evaluated once at registration
findings.description:
The `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` check moved from inside `onEvent` to around `manager.register(...)`. Registration happens once, in `DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.init()` (line 122) and `QuarkusKeycloakSessionFactory` (line 88).

- **Production:** equivalent, as long as the profile is fixed at startup.
- **Arquillian testsuite:** many tests toggle this feature at runtime with `@EnableFeature(value = ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, skipRestart = true)` (`UsersTest`, the token-exchange tests). In those runs the listener is never registered, so V1 permission cleanup on role, client and group removal silently stops.

This is an unrelated behavioural change in a feature PR; either revert it or justify it.

findings.title: Javadoc on the evaluator interfaces contradicts the code
findings.description:
- `requireManageMembers` (lines 132-135) says it throws when `canManageMembership` is false; the implementation checks `canManageMembers` (`GroupPermissions.java:376-379`).
- `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` (lines 142-147) documents "@return Stream" but returns a `Set`, and it actually checks `view-members`/`manage-members`, not `view`.
- `canView()` (lines 85-92) describes permission-based access without the "V2 only" qualifier used elsewhere; V1 `GroupPermissions.canView()` is role-only.
- `<p/>` is used throughout both interfaces; it is invalid Javadoc HTML and doclint flags self-closing elements.
- `@Deprecated` on `UserPermissionEvaluator.isImpersonatable` has no `@deprecated` note naming the replacement.

findings.title: New tests miss negative and all-groups paths and contain weak assertions
findings.description:
- **No test that `view` does not imply manage:** `testViewGroups` (lines 242-273) never tries to create or update a group after granting all-groups `VIEW`.
- **Uncovered paths:** all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members`, `/users/count`, sub-group listing (`GroupResource.getSubGroups`), and the V1 change where `canViewMembers` now also accepts `manage-members`.
- **Weak positive check:** `testManageGroupMembership` (lines 276-299) ends with `joinGroup` and no assertion that Bob is in the group.
- **Vacuous negative check:** the same test uses `joinGroup("no-such")`, which would not prove a permission denial if the lookup ran before the auth check.
- **Redundant status check and close:** lines 73-77, 191-195 and 255-259 assert 201 and wrap the response in try-with-resources, then call `ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse`, which now does both itself.
- **Nits:** stray `;;` at line 68, typo "initializaed" at line 70.

findings.title: `getOrCreateResource` now throws NPE on a null resource type; group names not resolved for display
findings.description: A `switch` on a `String` throws `NullPointerException` for `null`. Previously a null `resourceType` reached the descriptive `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object...")`. `throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided` guards only `ScopePermissionRepresentation`, so the import path (`RepresentationToModel.java:1423`) can reach this with null. Separately, `getResourceName` (line 334) still special-cases only `USERS`, so group permissions get no "All groups" or group-name label.

findings.title: `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` duplicates the `UserPermissionsV2` evaluation, minus one check
findings.description: The method is a near copy of `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` (lines 94-133) but drops the `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())` filter. Both V2 evaluators would be safer sharing one helper. Three V2 methods are also unsupported and throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, which makes the `extends GroupPermissions` relationship fragile; for example, the cleanup listener calls `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...)`.

findings.title: V1 `canViewMembers` now also accepts `manage-members`
findings.description: Folding `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` into `canViewMembers` changes V1 behaviour: `getAccess(group).viewMembers` now reports true for admins holding only `manage-members`. This looks intentional and matches the old `requireViewMembers`, but it is a behaviour change to the stable V1 path with no test.

findings.title: Remaining refactors are behaviour-preserving
findings.description:
- **Inlined role checks:** `canManageDefault`/`canViewDefault` are replaced by equivalent `root.hasOneAdminRole(...)` calls in `UserPermissions`, `GroupPermissions` and `RolePermissions.java:302`; no callers of the removed methods remain.
- **Removed duplicate filter:** the `canView` filter dropped from `UsersResource.searchForUser` is still applied in `toRepresentation` (`UsersResource.java:460`, `BruteForceUsersResource.java:160`).
- **Group ID guard:** the `!auth.users().canView()` guard is preserved inside `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`.
- **V2 user checks:** `UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles`/`canManageGroupMembership` are logically equivalent to the previous `canManage(user) || ...` form.
- **Test helper:** `ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse` now closes the response on assertion failure.
